title: Pre-2014 temperature slopes predicted the 2014-2016 heatwave change of southern California fish larvae, not of central California juvenile catches; the 2017-2019 change did not follow SST
abstract: Question: do per-taxon sea surface temperature (SST) slopes fitted before 2014 predict the change of fish assemblages during and after the 2014-2016 northeast Pacific marine heatwave (MHW)? Data: CalCOFI winter-spring fish larvae on the southern California core grid (1951-2023, 45 consistently identified taxa) and RREAS May-June midwater trawl juveniles in central California (1990-2025, 68 taxon-stage units), with ERSSTv5 regional SST. Methods: month and station effects were removed with training years only; slopes were fitted on years up to 2013; skill is the cross-taxon Spearman rho between observed and predicted changes (equal taxon weight), with taxon permutations, earlier warm events and placebo block pairs as references. Results: in CalCOFI the change from 2009-2013 to 2014-2016 followed the slopes (rho 0.56, Pearson r 0.64, p < 0.001, calibration slope 0.99), as well as or better than for four earlier warm events. In RREAS it did not (rho -0.12); RREAS slopes also failed for 1997-1998. In 2017-2019 SST decreased by 0.43 C, but taxa did not change back as predicted (rho 0.12 CalCOFI, -0.20 RREAS), unlike after the 1997-1998 El Nino (0.72, 0.32). RREAS was below all 7 placebo cooling pairs; CalCOFI was below 11 of 12 but similar to two earlier weak after-event windows. A model with current and two prior years of SST predicts the 2017-2019 change (rho 0.45, 0.37), consistent with a lagged response to six warm years. Effort-standardized CalCOFI spring richness was 1.4 SD above the SST prediction in 2015 and above it in all sampled years 2017-2022. Limitations: few events; the change form, equal weighting and rho were chosen after first results (all variants are reported); unscaled CalCOFI results are dominated by northern anchovy; new taxa are not tested; SST is the only driver tested.

citations.reason: Reports the CalCOFI larval fish response to the 2014-2016 heatwave as unprecedented; we test whether pre-2014 temperature slopes predict it.
